overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair controls public participation, so the Commission did not violate the law by not taking or reading public comments at the May 17 meeting. The AG declined to review public hearing law compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission failed to let several members of the public give verbal comments at a May 17 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the law gives the chair of the public body discretion to decide who may speak or otherwise participate during a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission did not acknowledge or read written comments submitted before the May 17 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, it is not a violation of the law for a public body to discuss or vote on a topic without first taking comments from the public.

allegations.summary: Complaint implicitly raised whether public hearing requirements for the 9 Sycamore Street matter were met; the AG said that is outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review, and offer no opinion on, whether any actions taken by the Commission could be a violation of any public hearing law or regulation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
